title: [Forests] Forest-Type Stratification Outperforms Hyperparameter Optimization for ICESat-2-Based Carbon Stock Estimation in Subtropical Forests
abstract: An accurate estimation of forest carbon stocks is essential for understanding the terrestrial carbon cycle and supporting climate change mitigation. ICESat-2 LiDAR provides globally consistent canopy structure information, but its application in heterogeneous subtropical forests remains challenging due to forest-type heterogeneity and the risk of optimistic accuracy estimates from inappropriate validation. This study aims to quantify the relative contributions of forest-type stratification and hyperparameter optimization to ICESat-2-based carbon stock estimation. Using Hangzhou, China, as a case study, we derived reference carbon densities from 2019 Forest Resource Inventory sub-compartments and matched each sub-compartment with the nearest ICESat-2 ATL08 segment. A three-stage modeling framework was designed using Random Forest: (A) global model with fixed hyperparameters; (B) global model with hyperparameters optimized via Optuna; and (C) forest-type-specific models using the same optimized hyperparameters. A nested cross-validation (fivefold outer, twofold inner) with paired validation samples was employed to prevent data leakage and ensure fair comparison. Results showed that forest-type stratification was the dominant driver of accuracy improvement, whereas global hyperparameter optimization provided only marginal gains. For mixed forest and evergreen broadleaf forest, type-specific models increased R2 from 0.34 to 0.63 and from 0.45 to 0.69, respectively. For bamboo forest, the global model completely failed (R2 < 0), while the type-specific model achieved R2 = 0.44 and reduced RMSE from 22.0 to 3.2 Mg C/ha. These findings demonstrate that in heterogeneous subtropical forests, stratifying by forest type should be prioritized over exhaustive hyperparameter tuning for ICESat-2-based carbon stock estimation.

title: [Remote Sensing] LD-DETR: A Multi-Scale Landslide Detection and Segmentation Network for Complex Geological Environments
abstract: Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards. High-resolution remote sensing imagery provides an effective means for landslide detection and mapping, supporting geological hazard assessment and early warning. However, existing methods still face challenges in complex mountainous scenes with heterogeneous land cover and geological conditions. These challenges include irregular segmentation boundaries caused by diverse landslide shapes, small-scale detection difficulties due to background interference, and foreground–background class imbalance that hinders effective model optimization. To address these issues, we propose LD-DETR, a network for landslide detection and segmentation. An Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module is integrated into the segmentation head to improve multi-scale feature representation, enabling better segmentation of landslides with varying spatial sizes. To alleviate class imbalance caused by the dominance of non-landslide pixels, a weighted Tversky Loss is introduced to improve the learning of hard samples. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is further combined with orientation-aware data augmentation to enable parameter-efficient adaptation, reducing the proportion of trainable parameters of LD-DETR to 41.07% while keeping the pre-trained backbone parameters frozen. Experiments on the Bijie and Luding Landslide Dataset (BLLD) demonstrate that LD-DETR is competitive with the baseline model and several YOLO-based approaches. The proposed method achieves an F1-score of 95.18% and a Recall of 95%, while the segmentation task reaches an mAP of 59.28%, slightly higher than the RF-DETR baseline. Furthermore, a limited-sample adaptation experiment on the Jiuzhai landslide dataset demonstrates the transferability of the proposed method across different geographic regions. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides competitive landslide detection and segmentation performance and offers an approach for fine-grained landslide mapping using remote sensing imagery.

title: WoodBR-Cross: A public wood-image dataset and individual-tree-disjoint benchmark for species identification
abstract: Wood-image benchmarks can yield optimistic estimates when images from the same tree occur in both training and test sets. WoodBR-Cross contains 4,875 transverse-surface images in 38 operational taxonomic classes, linked to 303 distinct trees identified by numeric catalogue witness codes (codigos-testemunho) in the Brazilian Forest Service collection. A species-level subset comprises 3,406 images, 20 classes and 214 trees. Three tasks compare duplicate-aware image partitions for all classes (A), image partitions for the species subset (B1), and individual-tree-disjoint partitions for that subset (B2). In B2, all images from each tree are kept together, so no tree is shared across training, validation or test within a fold. ResNet-50, ConvNeXt-Tiny and ViT-B/16 were evaluated with three outer folds, internal validation and five training seeds. Handcrafted and frozen-feature baselines complement border-only and randomized-label controls. Validation-selected ConvNeXt-Tiny achieved B2 tree-level macro-F1 of 0.8621 +/- 0.0317; frozen DINOv2 features yielded 0.9000 +/- 0.0722. Values are means and standard deviations across three seed-averaged fold means. Results estimate performance on previously unseen trees from this collection.

title: [Forests] Bibliometric Analysis of Remote Sensing and GIS Applications for Natural Resource Management in Forest Ecosystems
abstract: Sustainable management of natural resources requires tools that enable a comprehensive analysis of patterns of use, change and conservation of ecosystems. In this context, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Remote Sensing (RS) have established themselves as key technologies for analyzing and promoting the sustainable management of forest ecosystems and other natural resources. This study aimed to analyze the evolution, structure, and trends in scientific output regarding the use of GIS and remote sensing in natural resource management, with an emphasis on forest management, during the period from 1985 to 2025. A systematic bibliometric analysis was conducted using Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect, with the literature identification and selection process reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, yielding a final dataset of 679 documents. The results show sustained growth (5% annually), with an increase in citations. The output is concentrated in specialized journals and countries such as the United States and China. From a thematic perspective, the studies focus on forest ecosystems (81%), with a predominance of raster data use (91%). It is concluded that the research field is expanding, with significant advances since the year 2000, consolidating itself as a key area for the monitoring and sustainable management of forest resources. Likewise, the predominance of raster data use reflects an orientation toward large-scale spatial analyses, supported by open-access remote sensing platforms with continuous spatial coverage.

title: Beyond the Snowflakes: Disentangling Weather Effects from Confounding Meta-Factors in LiDAR Object Detection
abstract: Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) is critical for autonomous perception, yet its performance is known to degrade in adverse weather. While existing literature models snow as atmospheric noise that degrades performance, our granular evaluation on the WADS-3D and CADC datasets reveals a counter-intuitive phenomenon: detection accuracy consistently improves as snow intensity increases. Through ablation study and meta-information analysis, we reconcile this by confirming that while falling snow acts as noise, its negative impact is outweighed by a dominant, concurrent factor: significantly increased object point count. We hypothesize that this object point count boost acts as a geometric enhancement, driven by snow accumulation increasing vehicle surface area and a shift from specular to diffuse reflectance. Our findings demonstrate that evaluating perception systems using broad weather-severity bins without accounting for correlated object-level data can lead to misleading conclusions about detector robustness. We conclude that accurate evaluation requires decoupling atmospheric noise from surface accumulation effects and outline future research to validate these physical models. The WADS-3D dataset is available at: https://digitalcommons.mtu.edu/wads-3d/.

title: Desertification Forecasting in Semi-Arid Regions: Using Deep Learning to Probe the Observability Limits of Land Degradation Dynamics
abstract: Forecasting desertification has received far less attention than mapping it. We use a convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) trained on ten annual Earth Observation (EO) variables (2000-2023) over the semi-arid state of Ceará, Brazil, on a 256x206 grid at roughly 2.2 km resolution, to measure how much of the year-to-year evolution of a MapBiomas-derived degradation index (IDV) can be predicted from satellite data. The network predicts a bounded change on top of the last observed state, is trained in two stages (single-step, then recursive rollout) and is evaluated on a contiguous spatial and temporal holdout. State-wide mean IDV rose from 0.238 to 0.350 between 2000 and 2023, about 0.005 per year, but cell-level change is dominated by year-to-year jumps, and a gradient-boosting model given all channels explains only 4.7% of its variance. Against this ceiling, the ConvLSTM lowers RMSE relative to persistence by 1.6% one year ahead and 4.4% four years ahead in a held-out southern band (p < 0.001), beats persistence with a constant drift and reproduces 53-69% of the regional drift. Drift-aware baselines only help from the third year onward, by up to 4.4% in RMSE at six years. An earlier formulation that redrew the whole field each year predicted changes unrelated to the observed ones (correlation -0.06) and produced a spurious decline when run recursively. Channel knockouts suggest that elevation and EVI degrade the forecast, while slope and aspect have no measurable effect. Monte Carlo dropout and stochastic scenario maps convey the uncertainty that the expected-value forecast hides. Under climatological forcing, mean IDV rises from 0.350 in 2023 to 0.370 in 2030. EO-based desertification forecasting is therefore reliable for the regional trend, not for individual cells.

title: Detection of extremely rare dead cells in fluorescence microscopy images
abstract: Dead cell detection in fluorescence microscopy is essential for phenotypic screening and drug efficacy assessment. However, automated identification remains challenging due to signal variability, optical artifacts, and colocalization ambiguities across multiple channels. Markers that define nuclear boundaries do not neatly coincide spatially or temporally with apoptotic markers. Furthermore, marker accumulation kinetics vary across individual cells and apoptosis stages, making universal thresholds unreliable. We present a systematic comparison of several computational approaches for detecting apoptotic cells in nucleus-stained specimens: (1) heuristic methods using intensity thresholds, distributions, correlations, and domain guidance; (2) classification using numerical features (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM) and image features (ResNet-18 and EfficientNet-B0); and (3) anomaly detection, also using numerical features (Isolation Forest, one-class SVM and PCA reconstruction) and image features (convolutional autoencoders and Deep SVDD). Using a dataset of 258 images containing 65,527 cells/nuclei across multiple scenes with 243 manually annotated ground truth dead cells, we evaluate each method on metrics such as PR-AUC, Precision, Recall, F1-score, and macro-F1. Our results indicate that classification using image features (deep learning) and numerical features (traditional) achieved the best performance, with ResNet-18 and XGBoost significantly outperforming manually designed heuristics and anomaly detection methods. Our findings demonstrate that such biomedical problems remain highly challenging to solve even with the state-of-the-art computational and learning techniques. We aim to provide an effective decision-support tool to researchers while tackling such problems either fully-automatically or in a human-in-the-loop setting as an aide to domain scientists.

title: [Remote Sensing] Cross-Field Transfer of UAV-Based Winter Wheat Yield Prediction: Model Transferability and Sample Efficiency
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing is widely used for plot-scale crop yield prediction, but model performance may decline when models are transferred across fields with different crop, environmental, management, and sensing conditions. This study evaluated the cross-field transferability of UAV-based winter wheat yield models using multispectral (MS), RGB, and thermal infrared (TIR) information. Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models were evaluated under five strategies: target-only training (T1), direct transfer (T2), nitrogen-based adaptation (T3), cultivar-based adaptation (T4), and mixed adaptation (T5). Direct transfer increased the normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) from 12.7% to 14.0% for CatBoost and from 12.9% to 15.9% for MLP. Mixed adaptation achieved the best overall performance, with coefficient of determination (R2) values of 0.84 and 0.87 and NRMSE values of 11.7% and 10.9% for CatBoost and MLP, respectively. After controlling for calibration sample size, the difference between T3 and T4 became smaller, indicating that adaptation performance was influenced by both calibration-data composition and sample availability. CatBoost showed diminishing returns near the 40% calibration level in this experiment, whereas MLP continued to benefit from additional target-domain samples. Prediction errors were higher for samples beyond the source-domain yield range, while mixed adaptation reduced prediction errors in both yield-range groups. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and sensor-level ablation showed that MS features provided important predictive information, while RGB and TIR provided complementary information. These results indicate that target-domain adaptation can improve cross-field UAV yield prediction and highlight the importance of calibration design, yield-range mismatch, and multi-sensor information when transferring models to new fields.

title: Model-agnostic Knowledge Augmented Machine Learning for Weakly Annotated Bioimaging Data
abstract: Machine learning models are increasingly used for automated feature extraction from weakly annotated bioimaging data, such as microscopy and cytomorphology images. Due to the sole dependency of automated feature extraction, existing methods yield inconsistent classification performance across weakly annotated datasets. Here, we propose a model-agnostic knowledge augmentation method that enables ML models to exploit domain knowledge beyond what automated feature extraction can capture. The proposed approach improves classification performance across seven ML architectures. When integrated with masked autoencoder-based self-supervised learning, our method achieves the strongest overall performance, improving precision by 2.9% over the next-best method on three in-house microscopy datasets and by an average of 6.8% across three public cytomorphology benchmarks. We perform nucleus-level classification based on mislocalization of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, a phenotype linked to Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), using three independent microscopy datasets of motor neurons derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells. Accurate quantification of this phenotype at scale remains challenging and may contribute to inconsistencies across studies. Application of the best-performing model to these microscopy datasets reveals biological interpretations related to ALS, including dose-dependent effects of the proteasomal stressor, MG132, and the oxidative stressor, sodium arsenite (SA), on TDP-43 mislocalization, variable pathology in motor neurons from sporadic and familial ALS donors, and a lack of protection of the pharmacological compounds, edaravone and niclosamide, against SA-induced TDP-43 mislocalization. Together, our pipeline enables in-vitro cellular image analysis to advance understanding of ALS-associated pathology and potential treatments.

title: [Remote Sensing] High-Resolution Burned Area Mapping Using Sentinel-2 Imagery and Robust Satellite Techniques
abstract: High accuracy in burned area (BA) mapping is desirable for many fire-related applications. Most operational products are based on coarse-resolution satellite data with a final spatial resolution ranging from 250 m to 1000 m. The use of higher-resolution satellite data, such as that from the Multispectral Imager (MSI) on board Sentinel-2, is usually reserved for generating BA products only for specific countries and time periods. Moreover, BA algorithms are typically driven by fire detection products to minimize false identifications. The resulting accuracy of such BA products depends strongly on land cover, fire regime, and the reliability of the considered fire detection products. In this paper, we exploit the multitemporal Robust Satellite Technique (RST) to identify burned areas and implement a workflow based on Sentinel-2 images within Google Earth Engine. Test results from two complete region-wide experiments conducted under contrasting seasonal, phenological, and agricultural conditions showed that 97.85% of the mapped area was confirmed as burned within the adopted multi-source validation framework, with an area-based commission error of 1.38% and omission error of 0.60%. Missed detections documented by the Regional Spatial Data Infrastructure (RSDI) amounted to 10.60 ha, corresponding to approximately 0.9% of the burned area reported by RSDI over the tested periods. Polygon-level intercomparison with RSDI and the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) yielded Intersection over Union (IoU) values of 0.69 and 0.83, respectively. The proposed approach mapped larger burned areas than those reported by both RSDI (+48%) and EFFIS (+143%) as well.

title: [Remote Sensing] LuTan-1 InSAR-Constrained Reconstruction of Concealed Coal-Mining Working-Face Geometry
abstract: To address the difficulty in determining underground working face geometry when mining records are incomplete or mining activities are concealed, this study proposes an InSAR-constrained method for inverting the geometric parameters of concealed working faces. The method uses the line-of-sight (LOS) deformation field derived from LuTan-1 InSAR observations as the primary input. The search ranges of mining depth, mining thickness, coal seam dip angle, strike azimuth, working face center coordinates, strike length, and dip length are constrained using the morphology of the subsidence basin, available empirical parameters, and the Probability Integral Method (PIM). These constraints reduce the uncertainty caused by a large search space and parameter coupling in high-dimensional inversion. An adaptive multi-strategy differential evolution algorithm is then introduced. Latin hypercube sampling is used for population initialization. Dynamic parameter adjustment, multiple mutation strategies, reflective boundary handling, and local refinement are incorporated to improve optimization stability in complex parameter spaces. The simulation results show that the proposed method generally outperforms particle swarm optimization, genetic algorithm, evolutionary strategy, and standard differential evolution in inversion accuracy, convergence stability, and robustness to errors. It can reliably recover the main geometric parameters of a predefined working face. In the engineering case study of the 97,315 working face, the inverted active-mining geometry during the LuTan-1 observation period is generally consistent with the corresponding mine records, with a deformation-fitting RMSE of 32.53 mm and relative errors of the main geometric parameters below 7.9%. Parameter sensitivity analysis further shows that the geometric dimensions and center location of the working face have pronounced effects on the LOS deformation field. These parameters should therefore be tightly constrained during inversion. The results demonstrate that the proposed method provides a feasible remote-sensing approach for identifying concealed working faces and estimating goaf geometric parameters in mining areas with incomplete records.

title: [Remote Sensing] APFNet: An Adaptive Perception Fusion Network for Multi-Scale Object Detection in Remote Sensing
abstract: Accurate multi-scale object detection remains challenging in remote sensing (RS) imagery due to severe scale variation, limited pixel occupancy of small targets, and complex backgrounds. title: [Remote Sensing] Automatic Extraction of Discontinuity Traces from Rock Mass Point Cloud Data Using PhaseVote
abstract: Accurate and thorough detection of rock mass discontinuities is essential in geotechnical engineering as they have a significant impact on the stability of underground and surface excavations, yet they are difficult to automate. In the work reported here, an automatic algorithm, termed PhaseVote, is proposed for the extraction of discontinuity traces from the colour (RGB) attributes of 3D meshes which, combined with the region growing method, can help derive more accurate discontinuity modelling of a rock mass. Conventional edge detection methods degrade under low contrast and variable illumination, and geometry-based point-cloud methods overlook spectral features. The proposed approach uses contrast-invariant phase-based feature detection. The detected edges are filtered and then extended or pruned to form major discontinuity traces using the tensor voting method. The first algorithm, phase analysis, detects edges independently of local contrast, while the latter, tensor voting, links and denoises the resultant edge fragments into continuous traces using perceptual grouping. PhaseVote achieved detection rates of 94.85% and 84.72% and IoUs of 70.27% and 69.80%, compared with 76.12%/45.95% and 69.81%/43.81% for a conventional existing method. The results demonstrate that the proposed method is resilient to image contrast, robust to changes in the orientation of discontinuity planes, is less subjective and has a higher degree of automation.

title: Domain Adaptation of SAM 2.1 for Building-Component Segmentation in Image-Based 3D Reconstruction
abstract: 3D reconstruction of building components using image-based scanning requires appropriate segmentation of the objects in the 2D building images. In order to benefit from consistent grouping of the 2D masks in 3D environments, vision foundation models such as the Segment Anything Model have been utilized by Group Anything with Radiance Fields (GARField) to perform 3D segmentation. This study fine-tuned SAM 2.1 on the HBD dataset, consisting of 2,679 annotated images from 42 buildings, to enhance multi-class segmentation of 2D building images, covering 11 classes (Wall, Window, Ceiling, Door, Column, Beam, Floor, Opening, Curtain Wall, Roof, and Lift). The model was evaluated using per-class IoU, Dice, and mIoU metrics, and the results show an improvement in mIoU from 49.9% to 69.6%, indicating a meaningful improvement in class segmentation and providing a more accurate model for distilling the masks in 3D. The masks in the building images were grouped in the neural radiance field, and the pretrained SAM 2.1 was compared with the fine-tuned SAM 2.1 in the newly rendered images. This comparison shows that fine-tuning improves the grouping of building components at a user-selected grouping scale. This advances the application of Group Anything with Radiance Fields (GARField) in 3D, enabling better segmentation of building structures for 3D auto-reconstruction.

title: Revisiting the Task of Building Damage Assessment by Satellite Imaging
abstract: Natural disasters such as earthquakes, tropical storms, and floods cause extensive damage to buildings, and rapid, reliable damage maps are essential to guide emergency response. Automating this task, referred to as building damage assessment (BDA), from satellite imagery, has become an active research topic at the intersection of remote sensing, computer vision, and machine learning, particularly since supervised deep learning methods were shown to outperform earlier handcrafted approaches. Yet, despite a decade of intense activity and the release of several large-scale datasets, the field lacks a shared foundation. This chapter revisits the task of BDA from first principles, organized around three pillars: data, evaluation, and methods. We first clarify the candidate task for- mulations and argue for a sensor-agnostic, instance-based definition that tolerates missing pre-event imagery. We then review existing datasets along the axes of sensing modality, temporal configuration, and geographic coverage. On the evaluation side, we show that prevailing practices, largely based on a single aggregate score, are theoretically fragile, and we lay the foundations of a more informative, ranking-based, multi-score protocol. We further review methods ranging from task-specific deep networks to recent Earth observation foundation models, noticing that generalization to unseen events and regions remains an open difficulty. Finally, we discuss how these elements can inform the organization of a BDA challenge, including cross-validation, challenge, and private data-sharing setups designed to build trust between developers and users.

title: [Remote Sensing] Shape-Adaptive Learning and Style-Aware Decomposition for Domain-Generalized Oriented Object Detection
abstract: Oriented object detection is essential for interpreting high-resolution remote-sensing images, but detectors trained on a single source domain often suffer from severe performance degradation under unseen imaging conditions. Existing domain generalization methods mainly address horizontal detection or treat style variation as an undifferentiated perturbation, while the geometry-sensitive nature of oriented objects, especially elongated instances, is insufficiently considered. To address these limitations, a shape-adaptive learning and style-aware decomposition framework, termed SA-DGOD, is proposed for single-source domain-generalized oriented object detection. A frozen CLIP image encoder is employed only during training to provide multi-level style statistics, from which several interpretable branch-style pseudo-domains are constructed by modulating feature statistics that characterize photometric and contrast variations. These explicit pseudo-domain identities enable structured style diversification without accessing target-domain data. To improve orientation-sensitive representation learning, a shape-adaptive soft consistency loss is introduced for rotated RoI features. Instead of using a fixed-threshold binary weighting scheme, the proposed loss adopts an aspect-ratio-aware threshold and a continuous rotated-IoU-based weight, allowing elongated objects and geometrically reliable proposals to be handled more flexibly. Furthermore, a style-aware common-specific classifier decomposition is introduced into the proposed framework to separate domain-invariant category discrimination from pseudo-domain-specific style bias. Extensive experiments on multiple remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization capability of SA-DGOD.

title: Measurable Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting with Joint Region and Depth Supervision for Interactive Building Inspection
abstract: Image-based 3D reconstruction provides a scalable representation for building inspection and maintenance. However, photorealistic reconstruction alone does not fully provide the geometric measurability, semantic structure, and interactive information access required for engineering applications. This study proposes a measurable semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework with region and depth supervision for interactive building inspection from multi-view imagery. Mask-based region supervision suppresses irrelevant backgrounds and focuses optimization on target regions. Point-wise depth supervision guides Gaussian centers toward physical surfaces using reference geometry derived from multi-view stereo (MVS) point clouds, providing geometric anchors for measuring physical dimensions and areas. A semantic Gaussian field associates learnable class features with individual Gaussian primitives, enabling semantic rendering and component-level inspection. These capabilities are operationalized through AEC-SplatTwin, an interactive building inspection platform supporting real-time visualization, semantic analysis, quantitative measurement, and multimodal large language model (MLLM)-assisted interaction. On the synthetic UAV-inspection QuakeCity and smartphone-captured HKUPB datasets, the framework reduces Gaussian-center depth MAE by 58.1% and 86.8%, while its semantic field achieves mIoU values of 0.8529 and 0.8642. On HKUPB, the mean relative errors for height, width, and area measurements are 0.33%, 1.07%, and 0.60%. These results show that the proposed framework extends 3DGS beyond visual reconstruction into a measurable, semantically structured, and interactive engineering representation for building inspection.

title: [Remote Sensing] LiDAR-Assisted Survey Locates Unregistered Rock Shelters in the Blue Mountains, Australia
abstract: Rock shelters are important cultural and archaeological sites in Australia, often containing evidence of Aboriginal occupation and symbolic expression. While rock shelters have been investigated across Australia, locating them in rugged environments through pedestrian surveys remains challenging. This research contributes a methodology which integrates remote sensing, GIS analyses, and archaeological survey to locate rock shelters in the Blue Mountains. We produced models in ArcGIS Pro that analyse high-resolution, UAV-based LiDAR datasets and publicly available, low-resolution, aircraft-based LiDAR datasets from the New South Wales government. Our models yield locations of potential rock shelters, which can be visually evaluated in 3D LiDAR point clouds and ground-truthed through archaeological survey. Ground-truthing confirmed the successful detection of six known rock shelters on UAV and NSW LiDAR datasets, producing more accurate coordinates than the ones listed in online databases. Significantly, we identified three previously unregistered rock shelters that preserve rock art and lithics. These promising results indicate capacity to improve the spatial accuracy of legacy site records and locate unregistered archaeological rock shelters within, and potentially beyond, Australia. Our methodology promotes targeted and efficient survey of rock shelters that can produce regional datasets benefitting local communities, archaeology, and cultural heritage management.

title: Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning
abstract: Self-supervised learning on 3D medical images commonly relies on random sub-volume sampling during pretraining. However, random cropping implicitly treats all spatial regions as equally worth observing, despite anatomical priors and spatial redundancy that make regions inherently unequal in their value for representation learning. To this end, we first show through controlled crop-quality manipulations that better sub-volumes lead to better downstream transfer, revealing the observation policy as an overlooked bottleneck in 3D medical SSL. Motivated by this finding, we revisit sub-volume sampling as a \emph{where-to-look} problem. We propose \textbf{\method}, a plug-and-play framework that replaces random cropping with an offline coarse-to-fine probe bank guided by \textit{anatomy-awareness}, \textit{informativeness}, and \textit{diversity}. We instantiate \method as a lightweight \lite variant using geometric and image-statistical cues, and a diagnostic \feat variant using frozen visual features, to examine whether lightweight volume-intrinsic priors suffice or richer semantic cues reliably provide additional value. Extensive experiments across multiple 3D medical SSL backbones and downstream tasks demonstrate that \method-\lite consistently improves transfer performance over random sampling. Mechanistic analyses further attribute these gains to more anatomically plausible and informative observations, reduced spatial redundancy, more efficient learning dynamics, and more structured representations.

title: A Real-World CAD Segmentation Benchmark: Comparing Rule-Based and Learning-Based Approaches through Hole Detection
abstract: CAD segmentation datasets are predominantly synthetic or automatically labelled, leaving it unclear how well existing methods transfer to real-world engineering tasks. Fastener-relevant hole detection represents one such task, requiring human annotation and exhibiting greater geometric complexity than commonly used benchmarks. We address this gap through three main contributions. First, we develop two task-specific rule-based methods, one graph-wire-search and one multi-view based, and complement them with a human-annotated benchmark dataset derived from engineering CAD data that also enables training of UV-Net and AAGNet, representative learning-based approaches for B-Rep segmentation. Second, we conduct an extensive experimental study including parameter optimisation, evaluation on our benchmark dataset, cross-domain generalisation on a synthetic dataset, and an assessment of the feasibility of the approaches at varying dataset sizes and IoU thresholds. Third, we provide evidence-based insights into the strengths and limitations of different approaches: rule-based methods generalise well without training data, with the graph-wire-search method favouring recall and the multi-view method favouring precision, whereas learning-based methods achieve strong performance with sufficient annotations but exhibit reduced robustness under domain shift. These findings highlight trade-offs between data requirements, and robustness, and provide guidance not only for hole detection, but more broadly for real-world CAD segmentation tasks.

title: Selective Spatio-Temporal Fruit Inspector (S$^2$FI): A Mamba-based Framework for Rotational Fruit Quality Assessment
abstract: The global fruit and vegetable industry confronts severe post-harvest sorting challenges for small and medium-scale growers. Large intelligent sorting systems are too costly, while manual sorting suffers from low efficiency, inconsistent standards, and high labor demand. To bridge this gap between expensive equipment and inefficient manual work, this study develops a low-cost, high-efficiency, lightweight fruit sorting system driven by deep learning, suitable for small and medium growers. We propose the Selective Spatio-Temporal Fruit Inspector (S$^2$FI) architecture, which combines a 3D convolutional encoder with a Mamba-based backbone.It efficiently extracts spatiotemporal features, adaptively weighs informative frames during fruit rotation, and models long-range dependencies with linear complexity, reducing motion blur and occlusion. The hardware uses a dual-conveyor and curved rail design, supporting household power, fast deployment, and lightweight embedded deployment to improve affordability. We also built a conveyor-based fruit quality video dataset with 6,460 samples. Experiments on the held-out test set show that our method achieves the best trade-off among accuracy, efficiency, and practicality, outperforming the compared baselines on the test set, achieving an excellent balance of accuracy, speed, and practicality for real-world sorting.

title: [Remote Sensing] Estimating Downward Shortwave Radiation over Complex Terrain: Synergizing Sentinel-2 Imagery and Topographic Data via Physics-Guided XGBoost
abstract: Downward shortwave radiation (DSR) varies strongly across mountain slopes, and products designed for horizontal surfaces may not resolve this variability. We estimated slope-parallel DSR at eight Saihanba sites using Sentinel-2 imagery, topography, atmospheric inputs, and BRDF-informed surface albedo. Both branches used XGBoost, with the clear-sky branch further incorporating a parameterized radiation anchor, bounded residual learning, and support-aware output correction. On the 2024 test set (n = 1451), the full framework achieved an RMSE of 92.60 W/m2, an NRMSE of 15.79% and an R2 of 0.897. Pooled leave-one-site-out validation across all 6096 samples yielded an RMSE of 113.68 W/m2. For horizontal-surface observations at 10 Heihe River Basin stations, NRMSE was 17.60%. Clear-sky estimates depended most on solar-incidence geometry, whereas top-of-atmosphere spectra dominated the cloudy-sky XGBoost model.

title: [Remote Sensing] Seasonal Prior-Guided Dynamic Forecasting of Nonstationary Gridded PM2.5 Concentrations in China
abstract: Accurate and timely short-term forecasting of gridded PM2.5 concentrations is essential for air-quality management and public health protection, especially for the growing elderly population who are particularly vulnerable to air pollution. Advances in multi-source environmental data and deep learning have substantially improved the spatiotemporal prediction of PM2.5 concentrations. However, existing studies have mainly focused on developing increasingly sophisticated model architectures and optimization strategies while insufficiently considering the temporal nonstationarity of PM2.5 pollution and the recurrent characteristics associated with similar seasonal environmental regimes. Changes in natural environmental conditions and anthropogenic emissions can continuously alter the relationships governing PM2.5 concentrations, challenging the stability of continuous short-term forecasting; meanwhile, historically recurring seasonal pollution characteristics provide potentially valuable prior information for model adaptation. To address this problem, we propose a Seasonal Prior-guided Elastic Weight Consolidation (Seasonal EWC) framework for dynamic forecasting of nonstationary gridded PM2.5 concentrations in China. The framework derives season-specific parameter anchors and Fisher-based parameter importance from historical seasonal conditions and uses this prior knowledge to guide parameter updates during continuous short-term forecasting. Experiments with four representative spatiotemporal forecasting models showed that Seasonal EWC produced architecture-dependent changes in forecasting performance, reducing the annual mean MAE and RMSE by 30.3% and 31.7% for U-Net and by 10.9% and 7.6% for Earthformer, with only small improvements for IAM4VP and mixed changes for ConvLSTM. Parameter analysis revealed that Seasonal EWC reduced parameter-update magnitudes by approximately 27–32% and substantially limited long-term parameter deviation, indicating more stable adaptation during continuous forecasting. These findings demonstrate that seasonal prior knowledge can effectively guide dynamic model adaptation under evolving PM2.5 conditions, providing a promising approach for continuous short-term air-quality forecasting.

title: [Forests] Green Efficiency and Productivity Change in Wood Waste Utilization Across EU Countries: A Directional Distance Function Approach
abstract: Efficient wood waste utilization supports the circular bioeconomy, but comparative evidence on national treatment systems remains limited. title: MIRAGE: Metric Inference and Reliability-Aware Gaussian Estimation from Feed-Forward Vision
abstract: Feed-forward 3D priors enable high-quality reconstruction from image streams but often lack reliable metric scale and suffer from long-term trajectory drift. title: [Remote Sensing] PRIVER: Prompt-Stable Reciprocal Inter-Scale Visual Evidence Reranking for High-Resolution Remote-Sensing Imagery
abstract: High-resolution remote-sensing images contain dense object layouts and fine spatial details, but their spatial extent makes direct vision–language interpretation difficult. title: Tracking the Invisible: Self-Supervised Wheel Track Detection with Thermal-RGB Fusion
abstract: Accurate detection of drivable area is essential for autonomous driving and advanced driver assistance systems. While state-of-the-art methods focus on general traversability estimation, they prove inadequate for snow-covered roads where following existing wheel tracks offers crucial advantages: improved traction, predictable vehicle dynamics, and verified path stability. To address this, we propose a low-cost, self-supervised approach detecting safety-critical wheel tracks using synchronized RGB-I (RGB + Long-Wave Infrared) imagery. Our method automatically generates training labels by projecting future wheel trajectories from recorded GNSS data. A neural network is designed to identify wheel tracks with the 4-channel RGB-I images from challenging, white-out road surfaces. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in visually monotonous and featureless adverse environment, offering a robust and cost-effective alternative for winter autonomy. The newly introduced ThermalTrack dataset is available at: https://digitalcommons.mtu.edu/thermaltrack/.

title: [Remote Sensing] Reference Data Generation for Remote Sensing Image Classification: A Comprehensive Review of Methods, Challenges, and Recent Advances
abstract: Image classification is a fundamental technique that has been broadly adopted in remote sensing, computer vision and related areas. High-quality annotated datasets are necessary for the development and reliable evaluation of classification and segmentation algorithms for accurate thematic mapping. Reference data are critical in this sense, as their quality has a direct impact on the performance, accuracy and generalization of the model. However, generating reliable reference data remains challenging due to methodological, technical, and annotation-related uncertainties. This study reviews the principal challenges in reference data generation, and the solutions proposed in scientific literature. A total of 100 papers indexed in the Web of Science were examined. The review covers traditional reference data generation methods as well as emerging approaches based on semi-supervised, self-supervised, and active learning, segmentation- and post-processing-assisted labeling, benchmark dataset construction, sampling and accuracy assessment, and deep learning and automated label generation. Major challenges and emerging research directions are also discussed. The results indicate a clear shift from traditional manual techniques to more automated, learning based and accuracy driven methods. The study provides a framework of existing techniques and future research areas in image classification.

title: What Do Visual-Head Discovery Scores Actually Find? Attention Source, Necessity, and Random-Control Pitfalls in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Attention heads that attend to image regions relevant to a question are increasingly used to steer, ground and interpret vision-language models (VLMs) and to reduce their hallucinations. They are mostly found by ranking heads with an attention- pattern score and validated by steering or masking them. We ask how the choices inside such a discovery score shape the heads it returns, and which of the two validations identifies them. On Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct we vary the query type, the discovery corpus and the token positions whose attention is read (the attention source) in a full 2 x 3 x 2 design, and test all 12 head-sets for steerability (CERS: Contrastive Evidence-Region Steering score) and necessity (NCS: Necessity Con- trast Score) against layer-matched random head-sets. (1) The attention source and the query type reshape the selected heads far more than the corpus: changing the source keeps a median of 49 of the top-100 heads, the query 55 and the cor- pus 84, while two halves of the same data share 96-99. (2) Necessity follows the attention source: head-sets discovered from query-span attention are more nec- essary than last-token ones (difference 0.083, p=6 x 10^-10), and the two re- ferring + query-span sets lie 17-19 standard deviations above 250 layer-matched random sets (Holm-adjusted p=0.048). The referring + query-span effect re- plicates on several recent VLMs. (3) Steerability is not specific to the discovered heads: no discovered head-set steers better than its layer-matched random sets (rank p >= 0.14), and random sets drawn from the same or from any layer span the discovered sets' scores. Necessity therefore separates the discovery settings, while steering at this strength does not. We turn these findings into a protocol for reporting visual-head discoveries.

title: JMT-YOLO: Multi-task Domain Adaptation via Segmentation-Guided Consistency Learning
abstract: Domain adaptive object detection (DAOD) aims to reduce performance degradation due to distribution shifts between training (source) and testing (target) datasets. However, owing to insufficient modeling of fine-grained features and limited instance-level alignment, existing approaches become less effective under complex environmental conditions, such as extreme weather conditions and object occlusion. We overcome these challenges by proposing JMT-YOLO, a novel joint multi-task learning framework for DAOD. JMT-YOLO is based on the Mean Teacher architecture. It introduces an auxiliary semantic segmentation task and a masking mechanism to enhance the modeling of foreground-background semantic boundaries in the target domain. Specifically, fine-grained feature degradation is reduced by introducing a multiscale context-aware segmentation head equipped with a dense connection structure to effectively capture local and global contextual features. A mask-consistency loss is formulated by applying random masking operations to target images, thereby guiding the network to learn structural context and improving instance-level feature alignment. Extensive experiments on three benchmark domain adaptation tasks (Pascal VOC to Clipart1k, Cityscapes to Foggy Cityscapes, and KITTI to Cityscapes) demonstrate that JMT-YOLO achieves detection performances of 46.9%, 57.3%, and 61.0%, respectively. These results demonstrate superior performance over existing state-of-the-art and baseline methods, thereby validating the effectiveness and generalization of JMT-YOLO.

title: Structure-Aware Matching for Robust UAV Thermal-to-Satellite Geo-Localization
abstract: UAV thermal-to-satellite geo-localization localizes UAVs by matching real-time thermal images against georeferenced satellite images, enabling autonomous navigation in GNSS-denied and low-visibility conditions. However, substantial cross-modal disparities in color, brightness and viewpoint hinder conventional appearance-based methods from establishing reliable correspondences. While existing approaches predominantly address global modality shifts, they overlook the invariant scene structures inherently shared between thermal and satellite views. To bridge this gap, we propose SAMF, a Structure-Aware Matching Framework that explicitly exploits stable cross-modal structural cues to improve UAV thermal geolocalization. Specifically, the Directional Structure Enhancement Module (DSEM) strengthens robust structural representations by capturing directional and low-frequency spatial patterns, and the Modality-Aware Affine Remapping Module (MARM) subsequently applies affine correction to these enhanced features, further promoting cross-modal alignment. Additionally, we introduce the Thermal-UAV-Paired benchmark derived from the Thermal-UAV dataset. Extensive experiments on both the Boson-nighttime and Thermal-UAV-Paired datasets show that SAMF achieves state-of-the-art performance. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness and synergistic complementarity of DSEM and MARM. The code and dataset are released at: https://github.com/YuxinWang879/SAMF.git.

title: MemReg: Streaming Outdoor LiDAR Point Cloud Registration with Hybrid Memory Buffers
abstract: Prior outdoor LiDAR registration works are commonly limited by the pair-wise input paradigm, which neglects temporal correlations inherent within streaming sequences. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-frame outdoor point cloud registration network for streaming LiDAR scans enhanced with pose-related memory buffers. The key observation is that long-term temporal LiDAR sequences can provide rich global contextual information to complete sparse measurements, filter outliers, and address low-overlap problems, thereby boosting registration performance. Specifically, two hybrid memory buffers are designed, including an implicit memory feature buffer and an explicit memory pose buffer, to store and dynamically update pose-related temporal features. Moreover, a novel dynamic history weighting module is developed to adaptively fuse current and history pose-related features. Extensive experiments on three outdoor datasets, including KITTI, nuScenes, and Apollo-Southbay, demonstrate state-of-the-art performance of MemReg, surpassing all previous pair-wise methods and also multi-frame SLAM systems. Our method also generalizes surprisingly well to multiview indoor registration scenarios with rather competitive performance on 3DMatch, 3DLoMatch, and ScanNet. Code will be released at https://github.com/IRMVLab/MemReg.

title: [Remote Sensing] Adaptive Timing of Landslide Susceptibility Map Updates Using Persistent Deformation Changes
abstract: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) provides spatially extensive deformation measurements that support dynamic landslide susceptibility assessment. However, determining when landslide susceptibility maps require updating remains insufficiently studied. Three-observation confirmation and reference resetting allow update intervals to respond to both increasing and decreasing deformation. A common asymmetric matrix combines the current susceptibility class with the relative velocity change, allowing at most two upward steps or one downward step. We compared PDAR with no updating and fixed one-, three-, six- and twelve-month schedules across 6956 slope units in Yunyang, Kaizhou and Wushan. Baseline construction used 2013–2016, parameter calibration used 2017–2018, and evaluation covered 2019–2022. The fixed-window comparison showed that more frequent updating was not always beneficial. PDAR provides a state-dependent basis for selecting update windows rather than updating whenever newer observations become available.

title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
abstract: Interpreting machine learning model predictions is a central challenge, particularly for black-box vision models. Concept-based attribution methods interpret models using human-understandable concepts. Existing concept-based methods can only interpret classification and regression models. They require access to model weights or large concept-annotated datasets, and most methods cannot provide image-level attribution. We propose Hide and Seek (HnS), a new method for concept-level attribution that does not require access to model weights or labeled concept datasets. HnS can interpret a wide range of vision models. Given a concept and image set, HnS retrieves concept-aligned images using a vision-language model, localizes the concept within each image, masks the localized region, and measures attribution from the change in the black-box model's output between the original and masked images. This enables faithful attribution by directly measuring the model's behavior and supporting local attributions. We validated HnS on CelebA and COCO-Stuff. Compared to existing methods, HnS showed better agreement with ground-truth attributions. We demonstrated the applicability of HnS on diverse tasks, including image captioning and satellite image segmentation, where no existing concept attribution method can be used. We provided our anonymous code in the supplementary material.

title: [Remote Sensing] DCA-Net: Deep Context Aggregation Network for Remote Sensing Object Detection
abstract: Object detection in remote sensing scenarios faces multiple challenges, primarily manifested in multi-scale objects, class imbalance, densely packed small targets, and occlusion. To address these issues, we propose DCA-Net, an object detection method based on deep context aggregation. Built upon the YOLO architecture, the proposed method introduces parallel multi-branch pooling paths and an adaptive feature reweighting mechanism to construct a deep context aggregation backbone (DCA-Backbone). This enables efficient fusion and selective enhancement of multi-scale contextual semantic information. Furthermore, a detection head based on efficient channel interaction (ECI-Head) is designed to enhance the representational capability for multi-scale objects and complex morphological features. Experimental results demonstrate that DCA-Net achieves mAP50:95 of 50.5% on DIOR dataset and 61.5% on NWPU VHR-10 dataset, achieving competitive performance compared with other methods. Extensive visualization and ablation experiments further validate its detection accuracy and robustness in complex remote sensing scenarios.

title: Bridging Human and Model Attention: Explainability Analysis of CNN, Mamba, and ViT Architectures with Gaze-Based Validation
abstract: High-risk applications of deep learning require precise characterization of model decision-making. abstract: Geospatial foundation models can support disaster damage assessment, but high accuracy on familiar disasters may hide shortcut learning: prediction from event or scene characteristics rather than evidence that transfers to a new disaster. title: Thyroid Nodule Segmentation in Ultrasound Images with Conformal Uncertainty Estimation
abstract: Thyroid nodules affect a large proportion of the general population. Although most are benign, a non-negligible fraction is malignant. Ultrasound imaging is the primary diagnostic modality, and accurate nodule segmentation is a prerequisite for CAD systems to classify malignancy and assess metastatic risk.\\ In this work, we propose a thyroid nodule segmentation framework that integrates a DeepLabV3+, channel-attention modules and post-hoc conformal prediction, providing both accurate mask and pixel-level uncertainty estimates. We address thyroid ultrasound nodule segmentation as the first stage of a pipeline that also includes malignancy classification and metastatic risk prediction. We adopt DeepLabV3+, whose Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) captures multi-scale context, with an EfficientNet-B5 backbone for its accuracy-efficiency trade-off. Additionally, we test three channel-attention modules: Squeeze-and-Excitation, CBAM and Grouped Channel Attention (GCA), paired with two loss formulations (Dice-BCE and Boundary).\\ Since binary masks do not indicate prediction confidence, we wrap the trained model with a split conformal prediction layer that produces pixel-level uncertainty maps with statistical coverage guarantees.\\ We evaluate all configurations on the TN3K public benchmark using a fixed split and directly compare them with state-of-the-art methods. The plain backbone already improves upon previously reported results, with CBAM + Dice-BCE emerging as the best overall configuration.

title: UniDeblur: Unified Motion Deblurring via Fourier Convolution Learning
abstract: Image deblurring is a fundamental task in computer vision, yet existing methods mainly specialize in isolated scenarios. Consequently, the deblurring performance of these models drops significantly across scenarios with different cameras and image contents. This motivates the development of a unified motion deblurring framework that can handle diverse blur patterns. To this end, we construct a multi-source dataset and develop a data pruning and quality control pipeline. Then, to restore blur images with various motion blur kernels across different scenarios, we propose a unified motion deblurring framework via Fourier Convolution Learning. Existing deblurring networks usually rely on pixel-level mappings and overlook the convolutional nature of blur. Thus, the network mostly fits the image content itself rather than learning the convolution process, making it difficult to handle multi-source blur images. Instead of relying on spatial mapping, we perform blur-adaptive global filter learning in Fourier space, which avoids the limited spatial support of kernel estimation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our unified model effectively handles motion blurs across diverse sources and scenes, achieving competitive performance across both in-domain and OOD benchmarks. Code will be released at github.com/DeepMed-Lab-ECNU/Single-Image-Deblur.

title: [Remote Sensing] Soil Moisture Retrieval from Sentinel-1 SAR in Arid Oasis Regions: Error Analysis and Incidence Angle Effects
abstract: High-precision inversion of soil moisture content using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data still faces significant technical challenges, as the radar backscatter coefficient is influenced by complex interactions among surface roughness, vegetation cover, and soil permittivity. Therefore, systematically evaluating the mechanisms by which SAR system parameters and surface environmental variables influence soil moisture inversion is of critical scientific importance. This study utilized an improved alpha approximation algorithm in conjunction with Sentinel-1 SAR data to estimate soil moisture content for different land cover types in middle reaches of the Heihe River Basin and analyzed the sources of error in the soil moisture estimation process. The results indicate that the improved alpha approximation algorithm can achieve relatively satisfactory soil moisture inversion results. However, significant differences in the inversion results were still observed under different orbital and incidence angle conditions, with an average RMSE of 0.034 for ascending orbits and 0.037 for descending orbits. In desert regions, data from Ascending Orbit 128 with an incidence angle of 33° yielded the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE, 0.030 m3/m3) and the highest determination coefficient (R2, 0.848). In agricultural areas, the minimum RMSE for 2017 and 2018 was 0.030 m3/m3 and 0.041 m3/m3, respectively, while the maximum R2 values were 0.815 and 0.728, respectively; Compared with the desert region, the accuracy of soil moisture inversion in the agricultural region was reduced due to the influence of vegetation phenology and irrigation activities. Overall, the soil moisture inversion results for both study areas agreed well with field observations but still exhibited significant seasonal and interannual variations. The angle of incidence, surface roughness, vegetation dynamics, precipitation conditions, and irrigation activities were the primary factors affecting the accuracy of soil moisture inversion. Especially, the impact of the static roughness assumption on the accuracy of the alpha approximation algorithm is more pronounced.

title: [Remote Sensing] Joint Super-Resolution and Weighted Low-Rank Sparse Decomposition for Ground Penetrating Radar Clutter Suppression
abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is an important non-destructive sensing technology for subsurface detection. However, strong clutter from surface reflection and heterogeneous media often masks weak target responses in B-scan images. Existing low-rank and sparse decomposition (LRSD) methods, such as Robust Principal Component Analysis (RPCA), can separate clutter and targets but suffer from uniform singular value shrinkage and high computational cost; more critically, they operate only at the original resolution, refining only the spatial sampling grid of the migrated image under the inherent physical resolution limit. In this paper, we propose a Joint Super-Resolution and Weighted Low-Rank Sparse Decomposition (JSR-LRSD) framework that synergistically suppresses clutter and improves the spatial detail and target localization of the migrated image without extending its physical resolution. Unlike cascade approaches, which perform clutter removal first and super-resolution afterward and may amplify residual clutter, our method integrates a differentiable super-resolution network directly into the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) iterations. This allows for the sparse target matrix to be regularized by high-resolution image priors, while the high-resolution estimate adaptively adjusts the weighted nuclear norm via total variation feedback. An adaptive weighted nuclear norm is designed using singular values of the observed data and the total variation feedback from the high-resolution target estimate. A randomized singular value decomposition (SVD) is introduced to accelerate computation. Extensive experiments on simulated and laboratory GPR data demonstrate that the proposed JSR-LRSD achieves a higher signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) compared to conventional and LRSD-based methods, with clear improvement in spatial detail recovery, while maintaining computational efficiency.

title: Stochastic Finite-Transition Learning and Exploration for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
abstract: Generative MRI reconstruction maps an initial source distribution to the target image distribution along a learned recovery trajectory. Common generative methods, such as diffusion and flow, typically learn fine-grained local dynamics whose integration defines this global mapping, hence requiring many network evaluations at inference. Existing few-step sampling approaches can lower computational burden by approximating large transformations from local dynamics, albeit at the expense of reconstruction fidelity. FLEX-MRI instead partitions recovery into a small number of finite intervals between retained states defined by progressive changes in k-space support, and directly learns the reconstruction change across each interval. Because such finite transitions can admit multiple plausible outcomes, FLEX-MRI combines support-relaxed finite-transition learning with stochastic exploration. During training, randomized k-space sampling masks define finite-transition targets with varying support, while the prediction loss remains unrestricted by each individual mask. At inference, FLEX-MRI perturbs a random subset of currently estimated k-space coefficients, allowing the learned predictor to stochastically explore alternative transition paths. Each predicted state is then reconciled with the acquired measurements through data consistency. We theoretically show that this stochastic exploration induces nonzero transition-level variation through the learned recovery map and data consistency without requiring an auxiliary generative sampler. Experiments on multi-coil MRI datasets show that FLEX-MRI outperforms competing methods while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to few-step baselines.

title: Learning Holistic Scene Layout against View Shifts in Cross-View Geo-Localization
abstract: Cross-view geo-localization remains challenging due to drastic appearance variations and geometric distortions caused by viewpoint changes. Existing methods primarily rely on discriminative feature learning or explicit geometric alignment, yet often overlook an important observation: humans tend to match scenes by integrating the spatial context of multiple landmarks rather than relying solely on isolated local visual cues. Inspired by this, we propose a Spatial Context Modeling (SCM) module, which traverses feature maps along four orthogonal directions and models interactions among the resulting directional representations at each spatial position. By aggregating complementary directional observations, SCM constructs richer scene layout representations. Since reliable spatial context depends on robust visual features, we introduce a High-Frequency Information Guidance (HFIG) module that extracts stable structural cues from the frequency domain. By emphasizing edges and contours that are less sensitive to appearance variations, HFIG encourages the model to learn more robust representations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance on standard cross-view geo-localization benchmarks while exhibiting strong robustness under more challenging scenarios with unknown orientations and limited fields of view (FoVs).

title: SheafPrune: Sheaf-Guided Graph Propagation for Visual Token Pruning
abstract: Multimodal large language models process the complete visual token sequence, increasing prefill cost even when many tokens are irrelevant to the instruction. Token-wise saliency captures limited inter-token dependence; graph-based selection instead depends on how relations govern importance propagation and ranking. We study support-constrained propagation with node-degree correction. Inspired by sheaf geometry, SheafPrune uses modality-specific maps and a sparse text--visual graph to transfer relevance, then propagates scores on a separate visual graph and corrects them for degree. It retains a hard top-$k$ subset once before the frozen language model. The selector has about $4.5$M parameters and is trained end-to-end through the frozen LLaVA-NeXT-8B backbone using only the language-modeling objective. Explicit retention-ratio conditioning lets one checkpoint serve every budget. Across four backbones, ten benchmarks and seven pruning ratios, with all baselines re-implemented under one protocol, SheafPrune achieves the best retention at $22$ of $28$ backbone--budget settings, with monotonically growing margins in the moderate-to-aggressive regime. On LLaVA-NeXT, retaining $10\%$ of visual tokens yields a $5.15\times$ net prefill speedup and an $84.0\%$ end-to-end FLOPs reduction. Together with component ablations, these results support graph-constrained importance propagation and degree correction as a design for visual token selection across the evaluated backbones and tokenization schemes, improving the trade-off between accuracy retention and inference cost. code:https://github.com/Bob0817912/SheafPrune_ICLR_2027

title: [Remote Sensing] Multi-Index Remote Sensing Assessment of Agro-Climatic Change and Agricultural Responses in Temperate and Semi-Arid Regions
abstract: Diverse climatic regions exhibit unique agro-climatic vulnerabilities that are significantly shaped by climate stress. Understanding these distinct vulnerabilities is essential for developing effective policies to mitigate climate change impacts and ensuring sustainable environmental management. This study examines agro-climatic vulnerabilities in Nottinghamshire County (United Kingdom) and Udaipur District (India) from 2000 to 2024, comparing climate change impacts across temperate and semi-arid agricultural systems that represent fundamentally different system behaviours under contrasting climatic conditions. Using multi-temporal Landsat imagery and WorldClim climate data, nine environmental indices were analysed: the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), Moisture Stress Index (MSI), Land Surface Temperature (LST), Temperature Condition Index (TCI), Vegetation Health Index (VHI), Drought Risk Index (DRI), and Crop Health Index (CHI). The results reveal contrasting regional trajectories that challenge conventional assumptions about climate vulnerability. Udaipur exhibited improved vegetation and moisture conditions across the observation period, whereas Nottinghamshire showed intensifying moisture stress and declining precipitation. Warming was more pronounced in Nottinghamshire, while strong inter-index correlations validated the monitoring approach. These findings indicate that Udaipur benefits from intensified monsoon patterns, requiring flood mitigation and water-storage infrastructure, whereas Nottinghamshire’s rising moisture stress underscores the need for sustained monitoring and adaptive management. This comparative framework provides evidence-based insights for region-specific adaptation strategies essential to sustainable agricultural development across diverse agro-climatic zones.

title: Complexity-Calibrated Reconstruction Discrepancy for No-Reference Point Cloud Quality Assessment
abstract: The discrepancy induced by surface reconstruction in a distorted point cloud is jointly influenced by its intrinsic structural complexity and signal degradation. This observation motivates a referencefree point cloud quality assessment (PCQA) strategy that estimates and compensates for the complexity-induced component. We implement this strategy through successive reconstruction. Specifically, reconstructing the distorted point cloud produces an input-toreconstruction discrepancy that combines the effects of signal degradation and content complexity. Reapplying the reconstruction operator with stronger smoothing produces a discrepancy between successive reconstructions, which serves as a proxy for the complexityinduced component. This proxy is then used to calibrate the inputto-reconstruction discrepancy. We apply the same strategy to 3D geometry patches and their aligned 2D regions, enabling local comparison of the resulting discrepancies. The calibrated geometric and projected-view discrepancies are then fused into a final degradation score. For both branches, the discrepancies are measured using frozen pretrained perceptual representations. Our method does not require PCQA-specific training or fine-tuning. Experiments on three public databases show that the proposed method consistently outperforms most generic baselines and achieves performance comparable to several full-reference metrics.The code is available at https://github.com/HC-W-whc/CCRD-NR-PCQA.git.

title: Deep Learning Approach for RealTime Contraction Detection in Laboring Dairy Cattle
abstract: Currently, the animal production sector is undergoing rapid development of techniques that allow automatic monitoring of animal behaviour and health. This paper presents a computer vision-based approach for the automatic recognition of labor contractions in cows. During the course of the study, videos depicting 100 cow births were collected. From the obtained videos, 8500 cow contraction actions and about 25 000 non-contraction sequences were extracted which constituted the dataset. Leveraging image processing techniques and deep learning algorithms like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs), our methodology extracts relevant features from video frames to detect and classify contractions. Our study demonstrates a high accuracy rate of over 95% in detecting labor contractions. This automated system has the potential to enhance productivity and animal welfare in the dairy industry by providing real-time monitoring and facilitating timely intervention during difficult calvings. The video demonstration of the system can be found at the following URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8fTSG5D7dZ0

title: [Remote Sensing] Continuous Radar QPE Bias Field Reconstruction Through the Implicit Neural Representation Framework: QPE-BiasINR
abstract: Biases in high-spatiotemporal-resolution radar quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) can substantially compromise the reliability of meteorological and hydrological disaster warning. Existing QPE correction methods commonly assume predefined spatial smoothness, whereas localized biases can vary sharply over short spatial distances. We therefore propose an implicit neural representation (INR) framework for continuous radar QPE bias-field reconstruction (QPE-BiasINR). QPE-BiasINR introduces QPE-background modulation, which conditions bias estimation on the local precipitation context to account for precipitation-dependent spatial variations in radar QPE errors. Moreover, a multiscale spatial consistency (MSC) constraint is incorporated into the loss function to explicitly strengthen spatial consistency. title: When MLLMs miss what humans read: diagnosing and learning to read squint text
abstract: Multimodal LLMs can fail to read text embedded in an image's coarse structure (text a human recovers by squinting) and report that no text is present. title: [Remote Sensing] A Deep Learning Framework for Nonparametric SAR Autofocus Using a Hybrid Architecture
abstract: Autofocus plays a pivotal role in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging, which is particularly crucial for high-resolution applications. Traditional autofocus methods face inherent limitations, such as reliance on strong isolated scatterers within the scene or prohibitive computational complexity, making them inadequate for the practical demands of the rapid and batch processing of massive SAR imagery. Although recent deep learning (DL)-based methods have improved focusing efficiency, they predominantly rely on predefined high-order polynomial models for phase error estimation, which inevitably introduces parameter redundancy, restricts the model’s adaptability to complex phase errors, and is highly prone to inducing severe oscillations at the aperture boundaries. Subsequently, the self-attention mechanism of the Transformer is employed to capture the long-range dependencies across subapertures. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real measured satellite datasets demonstrate that, compared to traditional autofocus algorithms and existing DL-based methods, the proposed DeepAutofocus achieves superior focusing performance under various complex phase error conditions.

title: CUBE: Class-conditioned Unknown Boundary Evidence for Open-Set Insect Species Recognition
abstract: Open-set insect species recognition faces significant challenges when deployed in real-world biodiversity scenarios, particularly when encountering unknown species that are visually close to known training classes. Unlike generic out-of-distribution samples, fine-grained unknown insects are often not visually anomalous. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{Class-conditioned Unknown Boundary Evidence (CUBE)}, a novel evidence-based framework that models unknownness around each known species rather than as a single global unknown class. title: [Remote Sensing] Susceptibility Zoning of Seasonal Freeze–Thaw Deformation in Permafrost Subgrade Along the Qinghai–Tibet Highway
abstract: Permafrost subgrades along the Qinghai–Tibet Highway exhibit pronounced spatial variability in seasonal freeze–thaw deformation under the combined effects of complex permafrost conditions, climate change, and engineering disturbances. Focusing on the Xidatan–Tuojula Mountains section, this study integrated field monitoring, borehole investigations, subgrade geometric parameters, and multisource remote sensing data to establish a coupled ground–atmosphere model. The maximum refreezing depth (Hf) was selected as the susceptibility indicator, and an extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model based on 172 numerical simulations was developed to predict the spatial distribution of seasonal freeze–thaw deformation susceptibility at a 30 m resolution. The predicted susceptibility index was classified into five levels using the Jenks natural breaks method. The results show that susceptibility along the 532.20 km investigated section exhibits significant spatial heterogeneity. Level I sections account for the largest proportion (30.64%), followed by Level II (18.52%), Level IV (15.40%), Level V (9.54%), and Level III (7.92%). High-susceptibility sections are mainly concentrated in Hoh Xil, Wudaoliang, the Fenghuo Mountains, and the Tanggula Mountains, whereas low-susceptibility sections are primarily distributed in the Tuotuo River Basin, Tongtian River Basin, Wenquan Basin, and the Tuojula Mountains section. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified mean annual ground temperature (MAGT), subgrade height (SH), and ice content type (ICT) as the dominant controlling factors, contributing 51.59%, 26.56%, and 18.16%, respectively. The interactions between MAGT × SH and MAGT × ICT were identified as the dominant two-way interactions. These findings provide insights for identifying critical sections, optimizing monitoring strategies, and supporting zonation-based maintenance of permafrost highways.

title: MOSAIC: Multi-Scale Object-Centric Slot Adaptation with Image-Guided Prototype Conditioning for Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution
abstract: Pretrained diffusion Transformers provide powerful generative priors for image restoration, yet adapting them to structure-sensitive tasks remains challenging. We instantiate MOSAIC for remote sensing image super-resolution, where small objects, repetitive structures, and large-scale variation provide a challenging testbed. Experiments on UCMerced, AID, and RSSCN7 show consistent PSNR improvements across $\times 2$ and $\times 4$ settings and favorable LPIPS results at $\times 4$. Qualitative results further demonstrate improved preservation of small objects, structural boundaries, and repetitive spatial patterns.

title: Stride: Scale-Aware Multi-Agent Evolutionary Refinement for Infographic Generation
abstract: Infographic generation challenges text-to-image models because a single image must satisfy numerous visual, textual, and semantic constraints. We introduce Stride, a constraint-grounded multi-agent framework that treats refinement over any frozen generator as a history-aware evolution strategy. Stride separates constraint evaluation - whether each requirement is satisfied - from visual grounding - where and how it is violated. It then routes global revisions to a composer subagent and local corrections to a retoucher subagent. Each subagent conducts internal planning and generates multiple candidates, while Stride accepts a candidate only when it improves the verifier score, reducing regression across iterations. Because stochastic generators and imperfect verifiers make any single step unreliable, it is this combination of scale-aware routing, per-step redundancy, and monotonic acceptance that yields stable improvement across iterations. title: CompactSplat: Spatially Adaptive Gaussian Distribution for Feedforward Scene Reconstruction
abstract: Reconstructing 3D scenes from sparse views without per-scene optimization remains highly challenging, especially for recovering accurate geometry and fine textures. While recent feedforward approaches leverage generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for scene generation, they typically assign one or multiple Gaussians to each pixel.
